messages:
maria (eng-oncall): :rotating_light: getting paged — p99 spike on streaming in eu-west-1 since ~00:10 UTC. Alerts show degraded tail across int8 profiles.
incident-bot: Paging oncall: p95 420ms -> 900ms, p99 350ms -> 2.6s for route /v1/stream (eu-west-1). 17% streaming stalls in last 10m.
akshay (sre): noted, grabbing logs now. Any deploys or auto-rollouts around that time?
darren (infra): autocalib job finished at 00:08 UTC and started a gradual rollout of `auto-int8-eu-2026-03-15` profile. Canary looked fine but rollout hit 25% weight by 00:09.
sylvia (runtime): that profile changes kv-cache eviction and soft-quant thresholds for attention kernels. Could be tail regression under long contexts.
maria (eng-oncall): customers in EU complaining about streaming stalls (chat / long context). CS flagged two paying accounts experiencing disconnects.
customer-success-bot: Customer A (ACME corp) reported a service impact at 00:15 UTC — timeouts on long-chat sessions. Severity: high.
akshay (sre): can we confirm rollback or immediate fallback? What are safe mitigations?
sylvia (runtime): quick options: 1) Abort rollout (stop propagation), 2) Re-route traffic for streaming endpoints to fp32/fp16 variants, 3) Hotpatch runtime to force no-kv-evict for affected hosts. Fastest is abort + fallback routing.
darren (infra): aborting rollout now. `redwoodctl rollout abort --profile=auto-int8-eu-2026-03-15 --region=eu-west-1`
deploy-bot: Rollout abort accepted for `auto-int8-eu-2026-03-15` — rollback started (25% -> 0%). Progress: 0/4 batches remaining.
maria (eng-oncall): I'm going to pin the streaming production route to `model-x-fp16-v12` for eu-west until we validate. Doing a route switch: `redwoodctl route set /v1/stream --model=model-x-fp16-v12 --region=eu-west-1 --force`
darren (infra): route switch queued. Heads-up: small capacity hit, may increase cost but preserves profile.
akshay (sre): rolling capacity up + throttle suggestions: temporarily reduce max-streaming-concurrency to 60% for non-paid tiers to keep tails stable.
sylvia (runtime): collecting stack traces from affected pods. snippet from kernel logs (attention):
```
[00:09:58] attention_kernel: fallback path taken: dequant->repack latency spike, batch_size=1 seq=4096
[00:10:05] kvcache: eviction triggered during prefix replay, eviction_count=43
[00:10:06] stream_mux: stall detected, waiting for dequant job completion (t=1200ms)
```
maria (eng-oncall): good context. Looks like long sequences + dequant path causing blocking on the token loop.
akshay (sre): I'm opening an incident bridge and paging infra/runtime leads. Standby for oncall handoff in 10m.
incident-bot: Incident bridge created: https://redwood.incidents/bridge/INC-2999994311
akshay (sre): @sylvia please confirm if the fp16 hot path avoids the dequant blocking (we need perf numbers).
sylvia (runtime): yes — fp16 path uses fused attention kernels for long contexts; p99 for identical load in staging was 190ms.
darren (infra): abort complete. Rollout fully stopped at 00:18 UTC.
customer-success-bot: Customer A confirms partial recovery after 00:20 — fewer timeouts but some sessions still affected. They want an RCA and ETA.
maria (eng-oncall): we should do a phased verification: 1) route pinned, 2) soak 15m, 3) monitor p95/p99 and stall rate. If stalls drop under 3% proceed to full rollback and disable autocalib for region.
akshay (sre): starting automated verification dashboard: `monitoring.alerts.probes/streaming-tail` watching p95/p99/stalls.
sylvia (runtime): also recommend blocking that autocalib profile from future rollouts until we isolate the kv-eviction interaction: `redwoodctl profile lock --profile=auto-int8-eu-2026-03-15 --reason="fail-streaming-tail"`
darren (infra): locking profile now. Command returned OK.
maria (eng-oncall): status update at +20m: p95 back to ~140ms, p99 ~280ms, stall rate 2.1% — trending down. Customer A reports normal sessions resumed.
akshay (sre): good. We'll keep bridge open for another hour. Action items: - Syliva to collect perf diff and root cause hypothesis (kv-eviction + dequant hot path). - Darren to document rollout safeguards and tighten canary metrics for streaming routes. - Maria to follow up CS with mitigation timeline and apology.
sylvia (runtime): initial hypothesis: quant-profile reduced headroom for our fused kernels under long sequence lengths and triggered a fallback dequant path that interacts poorly with current kvcache eviction heuristics. I'll run a reproducer with seq=4096 and mixed batch shapes.
maria (eng-oncall): tagging summary for postmortem. Also we need to update the autocalib playbook to include 'do not auto-rollout to streaming routes without long-context canary'.
akshay (sre): agreed. I'll create the incident ticket (INC-2999994311) and assign owners.
incident-bot: INC-2999994311 created and assigned to `sylvia (runtime)`, priority P1.
darren (infra): FYI, we saw a small cost bump due to routing to fp16 and extra capacity, estimated +6% for the hour.
maria (eng-oncall): thanks everyone. keeping bridge open for final validation 45m. if p99 stabilizes under 400ms and stalls <3% we can close. :white_check_mark:
customer-success-bot: Logged note for Customer A: incident acknowledged, mitigation applied, follow-up scheduled with technical postmortem within 48h.
maria (eng-oncall): closing notes: do not re-enable `auto-int8-eu-2026-03-15` until runtime team posts regression test results.
